newsitem.title: MEXICO: John Deere sees '96 sales double year - ago.
newsitem.headline: John Deere sees '96 sales double year - ago.

text.p: Tractor-maker John Deere SA de CV is on course for sales of 6,200 units in 1996, compared to the 2,850 it sold in 1995, the company's CEO told Reuters.

"It's a substantial increase, albeit below 1993 and 1994 levels, when we were talking of 8,000 and 8,300 units," Luis Sada Gonzalez, chief executive at John Deere, said in an interview. Sada did not give details of what this would represent in terms of revenues for the company.
Market conditions during the third quarter of the year had been very favorable for the company, Sada said.
Sada also said that tractor sales had fallen dramatically since the seventies, and technical progress in Mexican farming had faltered particularly over the past 14 years.
There were currently 160,000 tractors throughout Mexico, which should be replaced every ten years, he said.
"We should be selling 16,000 units per year, which is what we used to sell in the seventies," he said.
Sada estimated that a backlog of 100,000 tractors had been accumulated in Mexico.
